text:
maria-support: Escalation from Cassie (CS). After the IdP keystore swap yesterday evening some customers report 401 at callback. ~10% of users hitting /sso/callback get 'Recipient mismatch' or 'Signature invalid'. Customer did a rolling cert rotate across multiple IdP nodes. :frowning_face:

cassie-cs: Customer says error started ~22:45 UTC, works for some users, fails for others (same browser, different network). They've already cleared local cookies, but repro persists for a subset of users.

kevin-eng: @maria-support can you paste a sample SAMLResponse (base64) or the assertion Recipient/ACS URL we saw in logs? Also which ACS URL do we expect on our side?

maria-support: Expected ACS: `https://app.customer.com/sso/callback`
Logs (redacted):
```
2026-03-15T22:46:02Z ERROR sso: verify_assertion: Recipient mismatch: got='https://app.customer.com/sso/callback/' expected='https://app.customer.com/sso/callback'
2026-03-15T22:46:02Z WARN sso: signature verification failed: fingerprint mismatch (sha256)
```
Attached sample SAMLResponse (base64) from failing user -> I decoded parts, assertion has ACS with trailing slash.

omar-sre: Hmm trailing slash causing Recipient compare to fail because we do strict string compare. But we also saw signature mismatch — suggests metadata used to verify signature didn't match public cert used by the IdP instance that signed this response. Could be old node with old cert still serving responses.

kevin-eng: Two hypotheses: 1) Mixed IdP fleet: some nodes still signed with old cert, new ones with rotated cert; metadata endpoint returned new cert but some nodes haven't swapped. 2) RelayState or proxy rewriting the callback (trailing slash) causing mismatch.

maria-support: Customer says their load balancer did a rolling keystore push; they believe metadata was updated centrally. They also have a CDN in front of the ACS endpoint (fastly) which rewrites trailing slashes sometimes.

kevin-eng: Can we ask them to do quick checks:
- curl the IdP metadata URL from multiple public IPs (to catch SHAs across nodes) and compare cert thumbprints. Example:
```
curl -s https://idp.customer.com/metadata | xmllint --xpath "//ds:X509Certificate/text()" - 2>/dev/null | sed -n '1p' | base64 --decode | sha256sum
```
- Grab raw SAMLResponse and run `xmlsec1 --verify` against both old and new certs if they have them.

maria-support: They're running commands now. Output shows two distinct cert thumbprints across different nodes (confirmed). One thumbprint matches the metadata, the other matches the old cert.

eng-oncall-bot: @kevin-eng This thread has been flagged high priority (P1) due to customer-facing 401s.

kevin-eng: Ok that confirms mixed fleet. Short-term mitigation: ask customer to ensure all IdP nodes are serving the SAME metadata/certchain and to avoid caching metadata at edge. Also we should make our Recipient comparison tolerant to trailing slash for next patch (low risk, helps interoperability). I'll open an eng runtime ticket.

omar-sre: For immediate customer workaround:
- Ask the IdP team to drain and update remaining nodes to the new keystore OR revert to old keystore until full rotation done.
- If CDN rewrites trailing slash, add a quick redirect rule to normalize `https://app.customer.com/sso/callback/` -> `.../sso/callback` (or vice versa) so Recipient matches exactly.

maria-support: Customer confirmed they rolled back keystore on the one lagging node and cleared any metadata caching on their edge caches. After ~5 minutes they reported success for previously failing users.

kevin-eng: Action items:
- eng: (KEVIN-5312) Add normalization for trailing slash in Recipient compare + add acceptance tests for common ACS variants.
- eng-infra/sre: (OMAR-742) Add warning in SSO logs when multiple IdP certs detected across metadata fetches (so we can surface that earlier).
- support: advise customers to avoid partial keystore rotation and to invalidate edge metadata caches during a cert swap.

cassie-cs: Customer thanked us and will coordinate a proper rotation window next week where they will rotate all nodes and purge CDNs.

maria-support: Closing the escalation — leaving P1 tag until changelist and infra alert are in flight. Will post links to PRs/tickets when available. :thumbsup:
